es: Identificar los personajes, la secuencia de hechos y los sentimientos de una canción narrativa.

teaching.en: The song tells the story of a girl and her grandfather.
teaching.es: La canción cuenta la historia de una niña y su abuelo.
teaching.explanationEs: Personajes: ¿quién aparece? Aquí, a girl y her grandfather.
segments: The song tells the story of
a girl and her grandfather.
teaching.audioText: The song tells the story of a girl and her grandfather.

teaching.en: In the first verse, the girl was never lonely because her grandfather sang every evening.
teaching.es: En la primera estrofa, la niña nunca se sentía sola porque su abuelo cantaba cada tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Sentimiento (was never lonely) + razón (because…).
segments: In the first verse, the girl was never
lonely because her grandfather sang every evening.
teaching.audioText: In the first verse, the girl was never lonely because her grandfather sang every evening.

teaching.en: The chorus repeats the main feeling: the girl misses the river.
teaching.es: El estribillo repite el sentimiento principal: la niña echa de menos el río.
teaching.explanationEs: El estribillo suele repetir la idea central de la canción.
segments: The chorus repeats the main feeling:
the girl misses the river.
teaching.audioText: The chorus repeats the main feeling: the girl misses the river.

teaching.en: The girl is the main character. She likes to sing by the river, and it is part of her memory.
teaching.es: La niña es el personaje principal. Le gusta cantar junto al río, y este es parte de su recuerdo.
teaching.explanationEs: Main character = personaje principal; memory = recuerdo.
segments: The girl is the main character. She likes to sing
by the river, and it is part of her memory.
teaching.audioText: The girl is the main character. She likes to sing by the river, and it is part of her memory.

teaching.en: Finally, she found his old letter and felt proud.
teaching.es: Por último, encontró su vieja carta y se sintió orgullosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Finally marca el último hecho; felt proud, el sentimiento final.
segments: Finally, she found his old
letter and felt proud.
teaching.audioText: Finally, she found his old letter and felt proud.

prompt.es: Lee la estrofa: ¿quiénes son los personajes de esta canción?

choices.text: a man and his teacher
a girl and her grandfather
two friends at school

feedback.es: Quien habla (I, una niña pequeña) y Grandpa son los personajes de la estrofa. No aparecen ni un maestro ni compañeros de escuela.

hint.es: Busca quién habla (I) y de quién habla.

origin.text: Every evening, Grandpa sang by the river. I was a little girl, and I was never alone.

prompt.es: Completa: «En la ciudad, la niña se sentía sola porque echaba de menos el río.»

feedback.es: Lonely es el sentimiento de quien no tiene compañía; because explica su razón: echaba de menos el río.

hint.es: Es un adjetivo de sentimiento: sin compañía.

origin.text: In the city, the girl felt ___ because she missed the river.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Al final, la niña se sintió orgullosa.»

feedback.es: El hecho final abre con finally y el sentimiento es felt proud.

hint.es: Empieza con la palabra que marca el último hecho.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista de la letra con lo que indica.

feedback.es: Cada pista marca un momento distinto de la secuencia: hábito, después, reciente y final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se sentía la narradora en la ciudad.

choices.text: She felt proud of the city.
She felt angry at the river.
She felt alone in the city.

feedback.es: No tenía amigos y echaba de menos el río: se sentía sola. Nada en el audio habla de orgullo ni de enfado.

origin.audio: Then I moved to a big city. I had no friends there, and I missed the river.

prompt.es: Según estas líneas, ¿qué hecho ocurrió más recientemente?

choices.text: She found his old letter.
Her grandfather sang by the river.
She moved to the city.

feedback.es: Last night marca el hecho más reciente: encontrar la carta. Las otras dos acciones ocurrieron antes.

origin.text: Every evening, Grandpa sang by the river. Then I moved to a big city. Last night I found his old letter.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién actuó en último lugar en el espectáculo.

choices.text: Leo
Sara
Mia

feedback.es: Finally marca el último hecho: Sara bailó al final. Mia cantó primero y Leo tocó la guitarra en medio.

origin.audio: The friends made a short show. First Mia sang, then Leo played the guitar, and finally Sara danced.

prompt.es: Según la letra, ¿por qué se sintió contenta la narradora al final?

choices.text: Because she got a new bus.
Because she learned a song.
Because her brother came back.

feedback.es: La razón está tras el último hecho: el hermano volvió por la tarde y por eso ella se sintió muy feliz.

origin.text: My brother left in the morning. I felt sad at the bus stop. He came back in the evening with a big smile. Then I felt so happy.

prompt.es: Completa: «La canción tiene tres estrofas y un estribillo.»

feedback.es: Hay tres estrofas (verses) y un estribillo (chorus) que se repite.

origin.text: The song has three ___ and one chorus.

prompt.es: Escribe el personaje, su sentimiento y la razón en una sola frase.

answer.text: The girl felt proud because she found the letter.
accepted: The girl felt proud because she found the letter.
The girl was proud because she found the letter.
She felt proud because she found the letter.
The girl felt proud because she found his letter.

feedback.es: La frase une personaje, sentimiento y razón con because: the girl + felt proud + because she found the letter.

origin.text: Datos: personaje = la niña; sentimiento = orgullosa; razón = encontró la carta.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase da una razón para el sentimiento del personaje?

choices.text: Leo was nervous because the show began soon.
Leo was nervous and the show began soon.
Leo was nervous, then the show began soon.

feedback.es: Because introduce la razón del sentimiento. And y then solo añaden otro dato o el orden de los hechos.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Luego la familia se mudó a otra ciudad.»

answer.text: Then the family moved to another city

feedback.es: Then marca el hecho siguiente y moved va en pasado porque la historia ya ocurrió.

prompt.es: Completa: «La canción es un recuerdo de un verano feliz.»

feedback.es: Memory es el recuerdo que la canción guarda, como el río de la historia.

origin.text: The song is a ___ of a happy summer.

title.es: La caja de herramientas del narrador

es: Elegir la forma adecuada para narrar: antecedente, costumbre pasada, hipótesis, relativa y discurso indirecto.

teaching.en: Before the storm arrived, Leo had closed all the windows.
teaching.es: Antes de que llegara la tormenta, Leo había cerrado todas las ventanas.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio: una acción anterior a otro hecho pasado.
segments: Before the storm arrived, Leo
had closed all the windows.
teaching.audioText: Before the storm arrived, Leo had closed all the windows.

teaching.en: It was a family habit: we used to sing in the car.
teaching.es: Era una costumbre familiar: solíamos cantar en el coche.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base: una costumbre pasada que ya no existe.
segments: It was a family habit: we
used to sing in the car.
teaching.audioText: It was a family habit: we used to sing in the car.

teaching.en: Mia feels a small regret: if she had taken her umbrella, she would have stayed dry.
teaching.es: Mia siente un pequeño arrepentimiento: si hubiera llevado su paraguas, se habría mantenido seca.
teaching.explanationEs: Tercer condicional: if + had + participio, would have + participio.
segments: Mia feels a small regret: if she had
taken her umbrella, she would have stayed dry.
teaching.audioText: Mia feels a small regret: if she had taken her umbrella, she would have stayed dry.

teaching.en: The neighbour who found the key gave it back to Leo.
teaching.es: El vecino que encontró la llave se la devolvió a Leo.
teaching.explanationEs: Who da información sobre una persona (which, sobre una cosa).
segments: The neighbour who found the key
gave it back to Leo.
teaching.audioText: The neighbour who found the key gave it back to Leo.

teaching.en: Mia told us that she had forgotten her umbrella.
teaching.es: Mia nos dijo que había olvidado su paraguas.
teaching.explanationEs: Told + persona + that: el verbo retrocede un paso (forgot → had forgotten).
segments: Mia told us that she
had forgotten her umbrella.
teaching.audioText: Mia told us that she had forgotten her umbrella.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando llegué, Ana ya se había ido.»

feedback.es: Después de had se usa el participio: Ana se había ido antes de que llegara el narrador.

hint.es: Hecho anterior a otro pasado: had + participio.

origin.text: When I arrived, Ana had already ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase habla de una costumbre del pasado que ya no existe?

choices.text: We had visited the river before the storm.
We visit the river every summer.
We used to visit the river every summer.

feedback.es: Used to + verbo base presenta una costumbre pasada. Had visited cuenta un hecho anterior y visit es presente.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Si hubiera llamado a Ana, habría oído la noticia.»

answer.text: If he had called Ana he would have heard the news

feedback.es: Tercer condicional: if + had + participio en la condición y would have + participio en el resultado.

hint.es: if + had + participio primero; would have + participio después.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con la idea que expresa.

pairs.es: algo que pasó antes de otro hecho

feedback.es: Cada forma cumple una función distinta: antecedente, costumbre, hipótesis y relativa.

pairs.es: algo que pasó antes de otro hecho

prompt.es: Completa: «La mujer que vive allí es mi tía.»

feedback.es: Para dar información sobre una persona se usa who (o that); which es para cosas.

origin.text: The woman ___ lives there is my aunt.

prompt.es: Leo dijo: «I finished the song.» ¿Cuál es el discurso indirecto correcto?

choices.text: Leo said that he had finished the song.
Leo said that he finishes the song.
Leo told that he had finished the song.

feedback.es: En discurso indirecto el verbo retrocede un paso: finished pasa a had finished. Told exige una persona detrás.

prompt.es: Completa las cuatro frases con la forma que falta.

feedback.es: Había limpiado (had), solía vivir (used to), si hubiéramos salido (had) y el hombre que vive (who): cada hueco pide su herramienta.

sentences: Before the party, Mia ___ already cleaned the house.
When Tom was small, he ___ to live near the sea.
If we ___ left earlier, we would have caught the bus.
The man ___ lives next door told me the news.

prompt.es: Sara dijo: «I lost my key.» ¿Qué frase lo cuenta bien después?

choices.text: Sara said me that she lost her key.
Sara told me that she had lost her key.
Sara told that she has lost her key.

feedback.es: Con told va una persona (told me) y el verbo retrocede: lost pasa a had lost. Las otras opciones mezclan said me o tiempos.

origin.text: Sara: «I lost my key.»

prompt.es: Escribe lo que habría pasado si Tom hubiera llevado un paraguas.

answer.text: If Tom had taken an umbrella, he would have stayed dry.
accepted: If Tom had taken an umbrella, he would have stayed dry.
If Tom had brought an umbrella, he would have stayed dry.
If Tom had taken an umbrella, he would not have got wet.

feedback.es: La hipótesis pasada lleva if + had + participio y would have + participio: if Tom had taken…, he would have stayed dry.

origin.text: Situación: Tom no llevó paraguas y se mojó. Escribe una hipótesis sobre el pasado.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mia dijo que había perdido la llave.»

answer.text: Mia said that she had lost the key

feedback.es: Said that + oración; el verbo retrocede un paso: lost pasa a had lost.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase usa bien who?

choices.text: The friend which called me lives in Quito.
The friend who he called me lives in Quito.
The friend who called me lives in Quito.

feedback.es: Who sustituye a la persona (the friend) sin repetir el sujeto. Which es para cosas y he sobra.

prompt.es: Completa: «El libro que leí la semana pasada era divertido.»

feedback.es: Para una cosa (the book) se usa which o that; who queda reservado para personas.

origin.text: The book ___ I read last week was funny.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta un hecho anterior a otro hecho pasado?

choices.text: The bus had left when we arrived.
The bus used to leave when we arrived.
The bus would leave when we arrived.

feedback.es: Had left es el antecedente: el autobús se fue antes de que llegáramos.

title.en: Follow a story in many voices
title.es: Seguir una historia en varias voces

es: Seguir una historia contada por varias voces e identificar quién dice qué y cuándo.

teaching.en: Each speaker tells a different version of the story with his or her own voice.
teaching.es: Cada hablante cuenta una versión distinta de la historia con su propia voz.
teaching.explanationEs: Each + singular: cada hablante aporta su propia versión.
segments: Each speaker tells a different version of the
story with his or her own voice.
teaching.audioText: Each speaker tells a different version of the story with his or her own voice.

teaching.en: Mia says that she closed the gate before dinner.
teaching.es: Mia dice que ella cerró el portón antes de la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Says that + oración: lo que cuenta Mia. Su «I» pasa a she.
segments: Mia says that she closed
the gate before dinner.
teaching.audioText: Mia says that she closed the gate before dinner.

teaching.en: Leo can't remember the time, but he saw one detail: the gate was open.
teaching.es: Leo no recuerda la hora, pero vio un detalle: el portón estaba abierto.
teaching.explanationEs: Un detalle concreto sirve para comparar versiones.
segments: Leo can't remember the time, but he
saw one detail: the gate was open.
teaching.audioText: Leo can't remember the time, but he saw one detail: the gate was open.

teaching.en: I agree with Leo: I saw Rex in the street at six.
teaching.es: Estoy de acuerdo con Leo: vi a Rex en la calle a las seis.
teaching.explanationEs: I = quien habla. Agree no lleva am: «estoy de acuerdo» es I agree.
segments: I agree with Leo: I saw
Rex in the street at six.
teaching.audioText: I agree with Leo: I saw Rex in the street at six.

teaching.en: Mia does not agree with Sara about the time.
teaching.es: Mia no está de acuerdo con Sara sobre la hora.
teaching.explanationEs: Agree with + persona: dos hablantes pueden contradecirse.
segments: Mia does not agree with
Sara about the time.
teaching.audioText: Mia does not agree with Sara about the time.

prompt.es: Lee las dos voces: ¿quién dice que vio el portón abierto?

choices.text: Leo
Mia
Nobody

feedback.es: Quien dice «I saw it open» es Leo. Mia cuenta otra cosa: que cerró el portón antes de la cena.

hint.es: Busca I + saw: es quien habla.

origin.text: Mia: I closed the gate before dinner. Leo: I saw it open at six.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia dice que ella cerró el portón.»

feedback.es: Al contar lo que dice Mia, su «I» pasa a she.

hint.es: Hablas de otra persona: cambia I por he o she.

origin.text: Mia says that ___ closed the gate.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sara está de acuerdo con Leo.»

feedback.es: Agree es un verbo en inglés: con Sara (she) se usa agrees, sin am ni is.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verbo con lo que expresa el hablante.

feedback.es: Cada verbo atribuye algo distinto: contar, recordar, opinar y coincidir.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién cree que el gato se llevó el pastel.

choices.text: Tom
Ana
Leo

feedback.es: El verbo thinks marca la opinión de Ana. Tom solo cuenta dónde dejó el pastel.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿quién no está de acuerdo con Carlos?

choices.text: Sara
Ana
Tom

feedback.es: Sara dice «I agree with Carlos», pero Tom contradice la hora. Ana no habla.

prompt.es: Escucha las tres voces y elige quién estaba en la cocina.

choices.text: Mia
Leo
Sara

prompt.es: Según las tres voces, ¿qué hecho ocurrió primero?

choices.text: Ana opened the box.
Sara saw Tom near the box.
Leo found the box empty.

feedback.es: Las horas ordenan los hechos: al mediodía (noon) Sara vio a Tom; después del almuerzo Ana abrió la caja; a las cuatro Leo la encontró vacía.

origin.text: Ana: I opened the box after lunch. Leo: I found the box empty at four. Sara: I saw Tom near the box at noon.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy de acuerdo con Tom.»

feedback.es: En inglés agree es un verbo: I agree. No se dice I am agree.

origin.text: I ___ with Tom.

accepted: Tom says that he found the key in the garden.
Tom says he found the key in the garden.
Tom said that he found the key in the garden.
Tom said he found the key in the garden.

feedback.es: Al contar lo que dijo otro, se usa Tom says that + oración, y su «I» pasa a he.

choices.text: Leo
Mia
Sara

prompt.es: Ordena: «Leo recuerda un detalle importante.»

feedback.es: El sujeto va primero y remembers lleva -s con Leo (he).

title.en: Draft a story with a twist

es: Escribir una historia breve con hábito, antecedente, giro, condicional y una frase contada.

teaching.en: Every Saturday, Sara used to walk past an old shop.
teaching.es: Cada sábado, Sara solía pasar delante de una tienda vieja.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base presenta la rutina al empezar la historia.
segments: Every Saturday, Sara used to
walk past an old shop.
teaching.audioText: Every Saturday, Sara used to walk past an old shop.

teaching.en: One day, she found a camera which her grandfather had lost years before.
teaching.es: Un día encontró una cámara que su abuelo había perdido años antes.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio: lo que había pasado antes del hecho principal.
segments: One day, she found a camera which
her grandfather had lost years before.
teaching.audioText: One day, she found a camera which her grandfather had lost years before.

teaching.en: Suddenly, she saw her own face in a photo. That was the twist.
teaching.es: De repente, vio su propia cara en una foto. Ese fue el giro.
teaching.explanationEs: Suddenly abre el giro; se usa con un pasado simple (saw).
segments: Suddenly, she saw her own face in
a photo. That was the twist.
teaching.audioText: Suddenly, she saw her own face in a photo. That was the twist.

teaching.en: If she had not entered the shop, she would never have found it.
teaching.es: Si no hubiera entrado en la tienda, nunca lo habría encontrado.
teaching.explanationEs: If + had + participio, would have + participio: lo que pudo pasar.
segments: If she had not entered the shop,
she would never have found it.
teaching.audioText: If she had not entered the shop, she would never have found it.

teaching.en: She told her mother that it was the best surprise of her life.
teaching.es: Le dijo a su madre que era la mejor sorpresa de su vida.
teaching.explanationEs: Told + persona + that: una frase contada dentro de la historia.
segments: She told her mother that it was
the best surprise of her life.
teaching.audioText: She told her mother that it was the best surprise of her life.

teaching.en: The ending gives a lesson: a small habit can change a life.
teaching.es: El final da una lección: un pequeño hábito puede cambiar una vida.
teaching.explanationEs: El final cierra con una reflexión.
segments: The ending gives a lesson: a
small habit can change a life.
teaching.audioText: The ending gives a lesson: a small habit can change a life.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué frase presentarías la rutina del personaje al empezar la historia?

choices.text: Every morning, Leo had walked to school.
Every morning, Leo used to walk to school.
Every morning, Leo would have walked to school.

feedback.es: Un antecedente lleva had + participio: had written (write, wrote, written).

feedback.es: Cada conector marca una parte de la historia: rutina, giro, hipótesis y final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el giro de esta historia.

choices.text: Leo stopped playing in the park.
A girl taught Leo a new song.

Leo used to walk his dog every afternoon. One day he found a key that his grandfather had hidden. Suddenly, the key opened an old door.

teaching.en: Someone asks a question, and I give a short answer with a reason.
teaching.es: Alguien hace una pregunta y doy una respuesta corta con una razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Respuesta corta + razón: así contestas al público.
segments: Someone asks a question, and I give
a short answer with a reason.
teaching.audioText: Someone asks a question, and I give a short answer with a reason.

teaching.en: She made a decision: she kept the camera because her grandfather had used it every summer.
teaching.es: Tomó una decisión: guardó la cámara porque su abuelo la había usado cada verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Because da la razón de una decisión; had used es un antecedente.
segments: She made a decision: she kept the camera
because her grandfather had used it every summer.
teaching.audioText: She made a decision: she kept the camera because her grandfather had used it every summer.

teaching.en: The reason is simple: she decided to keep the camera.
teaching.es: La razón es simple: decidió guardar la cámara.
teaching.explanationEs: Decide + to + verbo base (no «for keep»).
segments: The reason is simple: she
decided to keep the camera.
teaching.audioText: The reason is simple: she decided to keep the camera.

teaching.en: I finish with a tag: it was a big surprise, wasn't it?
teaching.es: Termino con una coletilla: fue una gran sorpresa, ¿verdad?
teaching.explanationEs: Frase afirmativa + coletilla negativa del mismo verbo.
segments: I finish with a tag: it
was a big surprise, wasn't it?
teaching.audioText: I finish with a tag: it was a big surprise, wasn't it?

teaching.en: The audience can agree: yes, it was.
teaching.es: El público puede estar de acuerdo: sí, lo fue.
teaching.explanationEs: La respuesta repite el verbo de la coletilla: yes, it was.
segments: The audience can agree:
yes, it was.
teaching.audioText: The audience can agree: yes, it was.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo abrirías una presentación ante el público?

choices.text: Good morning. I presented my story yesterday.
Good morning. I would have presented my story.
Good morning. I am going to present my story.

feedback.es: Para anunciar lo que harás ahora se usa be going to + verbo. Las otras opciones hablan del pasado o de una hipótesis.

hint.es: Anuncia lo que vas a hacer: be going to.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una sorpresa, ¿verdad?»

feedback.es: La coletilla repite el verbo de la frase y cambia de afirmativa a negativa: was → wasn't.

hint.es: Repite el verbo y hazlo negativo.

origin.text: It was a surprise, ___ it?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Decidió guardar la cámara.»

answer.text: She decided to keep the camera

feedback.es: Después de decided va to + verbo base: to keep.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pregunta del público con la respuesta que espera.

pairs.es: un momento: one day, last year

feedback.es: Cada pregunta pide un tipo de respuesta: razón, decisión, persona y momento.

pairs.es: un momento: one day, last year

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué guardó Tom la carta.

choices.text: It came from his grandmother.
It was a gift from a friend.
It had the address of a shop.

feedback.es: Sara da la razón tras because: su abuela la había escrito, es decir, venía de ella. Las otras razones no aparecen en el audio.

origin.audio: Someone in the audience asks: Why did Tom keep the letter? Sara answers: He kept it because his grandmother had written it.

prompt.es: Completa: «No, no la abrió.»

feedback.es: La respuesta corta repite el verbo de la coletilla: did she? → No, she didn't.

origin.text: She didn't open it, did she? No, she ___.

prompt.es: Escucha esta estrofa y elige cómo se sintió Leo mientras esperaba.

choices.text: He was proud of the train.
He was worried about the train.
He was tired of the station.

feedback.es: La estrofa dice que el tren llegaba muy tarde y Leo se sentía nervioso: estaba preocupado. Solo al final sonrió.

origin.audio: Leo waited at the station. The train was very late, and he felt nervous. Finally she arrived, and he smiled.

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases con la herramienta de narración.

feedback.es: Había contado (had told), solía contar (used to) y la niña que encontró (who): tres herramientas para narrar.

sentences: Before the class, Mia had already ___ the story to her mother.
When she was small, she ___ to tell stories every night.
The girl ___ found the camera is called Sara.

prompt.es: Según las tres voces, ¿quién no comparte la opinión de Sara?

choices.text: Leo
Sara
Tom

feedback.es: Sara y Leo coinciden en el amor por la familia; Tom contradice con otro motivo: el dinero.

origin.text: Sara: I think the girl kept the camera for love. Leo: I agree with Sara. Tom: No, I think she kept it for money.

prompt.es: Escribe una rutina y un giro para la historia de Tom y su abuela.

answer.text: Every Sunday, Tom used to cook with his grandmother. Suddenly, he found a recipe that she had written for him.
accepted: Every Sunday, Tom used to cook with his grandmother. Suddenly, he found a recipe that she had written for him.
Every Sunday, Tom used to cook with his grandmother. Suddenly, he found a recipe which she had written for him.
Tom used to cook with his grandmother every Sunday. Suddenly, he found a recipe that she had written for him.

feedback.es: La historia de dos frases combina rutina (used to), giro (suddenly) y antecedente (had written).

origin.text: Datos: cada domingo, Tom solía cocinar con su abuela; de repente, encontró una receta que ella había escrito para él.

prompt.es: Escribe la frase de cierre con coletilla: fue una historia muy divertida, ¿verdad?

answer.text: It was a very funny story, wasn't it?
accepted: It was a very funny story, wasn't it?
That was a very funny story, wasn't it?
It was a really funny story, wasn't it?

feedback.es: El cierre afirmativo lleva una coletilla negativa del mismo verbo: it was … wasn't it?

origin.text: Cierre: fue una historia muy divertida, ¿verdad?

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta del presentador al público es correcta?

choices.text: He decided to call his aunt.
He decided for call his aunt.
He decided calling his aunt.

feedback.es: Después de decided se usa to + verbo base: decided to call. For + verbo y la forma -ing no encajan.

origin.text: Audience: What did Leo decide to do?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Porque su abuela la había usado.»

answer.text: Because her grandmother had used it

feedback.es: La respuesta con razón abre con because y usa had used para el antecedente.
